sources.text: Show HN: Tracon (air traffic control for subagents) | Hacker News Hacker News new | past | comments | ask | show | jobs | submit login Show HN: Tracon (air traffic control for subagents) ( github.com/phalladar ) 1 point by allocate 1 hour ago | hide | past | favorite | discuss My Claude Code workflow usually involves... a lot of subagents. I make one Opus model coordinate work as my tech lead, it dispatches subagents using models appropriate for the task into their own git worktrees, and then I try to multitask and do something else while they run. I'd been finding lately (particularly with Opus 5.5) that there was a ton of drift and instances of subagents not doing anything and it was evading the attention of the TL despite the instructions I gave it to have them report in at a regular cadence. Running tracon in a split terminal is my new personal workflow. It gives me early indicators when things start going off the rails (ex. blocked on a prompt, idle, looping on a failing command, simultaneous edits to files other subagents are editing, drifting off the brief, etc.) and I can interrogate the subagent's workflow and by pressing n the main agent gets a note to make a call on how and if to correct it. Read-only and runs on your machine: it tails transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/ and checks each worktree with ps, lsof, and git -- only thing that leaves your machine is what the Haiku judge reads for classification (or optionally you can turn that off with --no-judge). I've found it super useful for the game I'm building and figured others in the community might also find it useful. If you just want to give it a spin without committing: uvx tracon --demo macOS and Linux, Python 3.12+, MIT. (Not affiliated with Anthropic.) help Consider applying for YC's Winter 2027 batch! sources.text: # tracon **Air traffic control for parallel Claude Code subagents.** A live terminal and browser monitor that spots stuck, blocked and drifting agents, and the worktree file conflicts headed for your merge. [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/tracon)](https://pypi.org/project/tracon/) [![Python 3.12+](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/tracon)](https://pypi.org/project/tracon/) [![tests](https://github.com/phalladar/tracon/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/phalladar/tracon/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ![A terminal split in two. On the left, a Claude Code session is asked to /expedite checkout-v2 and dispatches seven worktree agents. On the right, tracon lists them as they start; over the run one agent is blocked on a permission prompt, one goes idle, one drifts off its brief and one is stuck retrying a failing command. The user selects the stuck agent in tracon, presses n to nudge the lead with a drafted note; it arrives in the Claude Code session, the lead messages the agent, and tracon shows it back on track.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phalladar/tracon/main/docs/screenshots/hero.gif) Left: a Claude Code session orchestrating seven worktree agents. Right: tracon in a split next to it. A made-up run from tracon --demo , sped up. ```sh uvx tracon --demo # look around a made-up run; no Claude Code session needed uvx tracon # watch the Claude Code session in the next split, else your newest with subagents ``` You dispatched six agents an hour ago. One has been waiting 40 minutes on a permission prompt nobody can see. Two are editing `shop/cart.py` at the same time. One is restyling the admin pages its brief said to leave alone, and another has run the same failing command six times. Claude Code's status line shows none of it. Like a [TRACON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminal_radar_approach_control_facilities) controller watching every aircraft on one scope, `tracon` shows every agent at once: what it is doing, whether it is holding, whether it has drifted off its brief, and whether two of them are on a collision course in the same file. Run it in a split next to your session. - **Read-only and local.** It reads the transcripts Claude Code already writes to disk and never writes to your repository. It sends something to a session only when you press `n`. See [What it touches](#what-it-touches). - **No setup.** No hooks, no config, no account. Start it in a split next to your session and it finds that session. - **Optional LLM judge.** A small model checks each busy agent against its brief, for about a tenth of a cent a check, with a hard per-run budget. `--no-judge` turns it off. > tracon is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by > Anthropic. "Claude" and "Claude Code" are trademarks of Anthropic. ## What it catches ### Every agent on one scope Agents waiting on a permission prompt nobody can answer, agents that went quiet, hung test runs, processes left behind, loops, edits to the wrong checkout or on a stale base, two agents changing the same file, and (with the optional [judge](#the-judge-optional-on-by-default)) agents drifting from their brief. Red needs you now; amber is worth a look. ![tracon's terminal view: a table of agents with states BLOCKED, IDLE, RUNNING and WORKING, judge verdicts on track, drifting and stuck, and flags such as LOOP, COLLIDE and STALE-BASE; below it, the selected agent's feed of repeated connection-refused errors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phalladar/tracon/main/docs/screenshots/tui-overview.png) ### Why one is in trouble `enter` opens an agent: what it is doing, the judge's concern and how the verdict changed, every flag explained, the files it touched outside its brief, and a live tail of what it said, in full. The tool calls between two messages fold into one line (`▸ 23 tool calls Read 5 · Edit 8 …`); click it to open that run, or press `e` to open them all. ![tracon's detail view of an agent the judge marks as drifting: it has edited admin files its brief says to leave alone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phalladar/tracon/main/docs/screenshots/tui-detail.png) ### Merge conflicts before the merge `x` shows which agent edited which file. `!` marks a file two agents were editing at the same time. ![tracon's files heatmap: rows of files, one column per agent, with two agents both editing shop/cart.py marked with an exclamation mark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phalladar/tracon/main/docs/screenshots/tui-files.png) ### Nudge the lead in one key `n` nudges your orchestrating session about the selected agent: tracon drafts a note with the agent's state, flags, the judge's concern and what to do, and sends it straight away (see [Nudging the lead](#nudging-the-lead)). ### Replay the whole run `t` is the timeline. `[` and `]` rewind and forward, `space` plays it back, and `--at "07:20"` opens any past session as it stood at that time. ![tracon's terminal timeline: one row per agent, coloured by edits, shell calls and reads, with silent stretches dotted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phalladar/tracon/main/docs/screenshots/tui-timeline.png) [Reading the screen](#reading-the-screen) lists every state and flag, what it means, and what to do about it. With `--notify`, a desktop notification fires when an agent needs you. The terminal title is set to the watched session's name (`◎ `, mirroring Claude Code's `✳ `), so the split reads as part of that session. ## Install Requires Python 3.12+, on macOS or Linux. ```sh uv tool install tracon # or: pipx install tracon uv tool install 'tracon[api]' # optional: judge through the Anthropic API instead of `claude -p` ``` Or run it without installing: `uvx tracon`. From source: ```sh git clone https://github.com/phalladar/tracon && cd tracon uv tool install --editable . ``` ## Use ```sh cd your-project && tracon # the session in the next split, else the newest in this project (or anywhere) tracon --demo # a made-up run, to look around tracon web # browser view only tracon --list # recent sessions that spawned subagents tracon -s 4f2a # pick a session by id prefix tracon --at "2026-10-11 07:20" # replay a session as it stood at that time tracon --once # print one snapshot and exit tracon --once --json # snapshot as JSON (for scripts and status bars) ``` A good layout: your orchestrating session on one side, `tracon` in a split next to it (in Ghostty, `cmd+d`). Without `--session`, tracon picks, in order: 1. the Claude Code session in a split of the same tab (Ghostty 1.3+ on macOS), matched by the name Claude Code gives its terminal, even before it has started any subagents; 2. the newest session with subagents in this folder's project, or in the nearest parent folder that has one; 3. the newest session with subagents anywhere. It keeps checking: when the session in the next split changes, or a new session with subagents takes the top spot, tracon switches to it. Picking a session with `s` stops that. ### Terminal keys | Key | | |---|---| | `enter` | agent detail: state, judge verdict, flags, files, live processes, and what the agent said, with the lead's messages and its tool calls folded between them (`e` or a click unfolds them) | | `e` | open or fold every run of tool calls, in the pane under the table and in the detail (a click on `▸` does one) | | `t` | timeline: every agent across the run, coloured by activity, with the lead's merges and messages | | `x` | files heatmap: which agents edited which files, concurrent edits marked `!` | | `w` | open the browser view | | `j` | ask the judge about the selected agent now | | `d` | dismiss the judge's drifting or stuck verdict on the selected agent (press again to restore) | | `n` | nudge the lead about the selected agent: sends a note with its state, flags and what to do (live only) | | `[` `]` / `{` `}` | rewind / forward 5 / 30 min (enters replay) · `space` play · `l` back to live | | `o` / `c` | open the agent's worktree in a new terminal window (Ghostty if installed) / copy its path | | `s` | sessions, last active first: pick one to watch (stops following the next split and new sessions) | | `h` / `q` | hide finished agents / quit | ### Browser view `w` in the terminal, or `tracon web`, serves a page on `127.0.0.1`: ![The tracon browser timeline replaying a run: seven subagents spawn and work, coloured by edits, shell calls and reads, with judge verdicts per agent and the lead's merges and messages along the top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phalladar/tracon/main/docs/screenshots/replay.gif) - **Timeline**: zoom with the scroll wheel, drag to pan, double-click to fit. Hover any bar for the calls it covers. Silent stretches past the idle threshold are drawn in orange. - **Files**: heatmap of edits per file per agent, shared files first. - **Replay scrubber**: drag through the run, or press ▶ to play it back. - Click an agent for its detail drawer and live activity feed. ## Reading the screen Each agent row has a **state** (what it is doing now), a **JUDGE** column (the LLM's read of whether it is on brief), and any number of **flags** (things worth a look). Press `enter` on a row for the detail, which shows the judge's one-line concern and every flag's explanation. You don't control agents from tracon; it is read-only. When something needs action, you act in your orchestrating session: answer the prompt there, or ask the lead to message, stop or re-dispatch the agent. ### Columns | Column | Shows | |---|---| | **STATE** | What it is doing now (below) | | **TASK** | The description the lead gave the agent; the pinned row is the lead itself | | **MODEL** | The model it runs on | | **JUDGE** | The judge's latest verdict (below) | | **NOW** | Its current or latest action | | **QUIET** | Time since its transcript last moved; red past the 5 min idle threshold | | **RUN** | Time since it started | | **CONTEXT** | Context size in tokens; amber above 300k, red above 450k | | **EDITS** | Files it edited; `(n⚑)` counts those the brief never names | | **COMMITS** | `git commit` calls it made | | **MSGS** | Messages the lead sent it | | **FLAGS** | Things worth a look (below) | ### Colours | Colour | Browser label | Means | |---|---|---| | red | Needs you | act now: the agent can't continue, or is doing damage | | amber | Check | have a look when you can; often fine | | green | Working | nothing to do | | grey | Done / Note | finished, or history kept for context | Once an agent has finished, its flags turn grey: they are history, not action. Only **OUTSIDE** and **ORPHAN** stay loud, because what they describe outlives the agent. ### States | State | Means | What to do | |---|---|---| | **BLOCKED** | An instant call (Edit, Read, `git status`) has been open for 45 s, or a shell call with nothing running: it is waiting on a permission prompt | Answer the prompt if it is showing in your session. If nobody can see it, allow that tool in your permission settings, or have the lead stop and re-dispatch the agent | | **IDLE** | No transcript activity for 5 min and nothing running | Check the last lines of its feed: it often hit an error or is waiting for input it will never get. Have the lead message it or stop it | | **STALLED** | A process has run for 20 min with no file change or commit | Usually a hung test or a watcher that never exits. Check the process in the detail; kill it, or have the lead stop the agent | | **ORPHANED** | Silent, but a detached process it started is still running after its parent died | Kill the process (pid in the detail) | | **WAITING** | Its turn has ended (or it is quiet) while background work it launched still runs | Usually nothing: it resumes when that work finishes. If the work is stuck, see STALLED | | **PENDING** | Replay only: a tool call was open, and without process data tracon can't tell a long run from a prompt | Nothing; go live to see which it is | | **RUNNING** | A tool call is in progress (a build, a test run) | Nothing | | **WORKING** | Making calls normally | Nothing | | **STARTING** | Dispatched, no activity yet | Nothing | | **DONE** | Finished: handed back a report, the lead was told it completed, or it ended with a final answer and nothing running | Read its report; merge | | **STOPPED** | Stopped by the lead, failed, or killed | Check why if you didn't expect it | A pinned **◆ lead** row shows the orchestrating session itself (running, working, or waiting on its agents or on you), so its activity is never mistaken for a subagent's. ### Flags | Flag | Means | What to do | |---|---|---| | **LOOP** | The same call 3× in a row with no edit in between | It is spinning. Have the lead tell it what it is missing, or stop it | | **ERRORS** | Its last 3 tool calls failed | Look at the errors in the feed; it may recover on its own | | **DENIED** | Tool calls were denied, with the classifier's reasons (e.g. "Modify Shared Resources"), or refused by a guard (Claude Code's worktree isolation or its sleep block, which say what to do instead). A denial is amber for 30 min, then grey. A guard refusal stays grey while the agent's next call gets through, and turns amber only when it is refused twice in a row | For a denial, decide whether it should have that permission; if so, allow it and have the lead tell it to retry. For an amber refusal, have the lead tell it to do what the refusal says, or to report what it can't do | | **OUTSIDE** | A worktree agent edited the main checkout instead of its worktree | Check `git status` in your main checkout and undo or move those edits | | **BRANCH** | Its worktree is on a different branch from the one it was given | Check it hasn't committed to the wrong branch before you merge | | **STALE-BASE** | It started editing before merging the base branch, after the lead had already merged something. Live, git has the last word: no flag once its HEAD contains the base, and the flag says how many commits behind it is | Expect conflicts; have it merge the base before it goes further | | **COLLIDE** | Another agent edited the same file while both were running. Press `x` for the heatmap | The second merge may conflict. Decide which agent owns the file, or plan the merge order | | **OFF-BRIEF** | It edited files the brief never names (grey: often legitimate) | Glance at the list; worth a question only if the files look unrelated | | **BG** | It launched background or detached runs. Amber when its brief says to run in the foreground and nowhere allows a background or `nohup` run | If amber, it is ignoring the brief; have the lead remind it | | **UNCOMMITTED** | Edits left uncommitted for 45 min | Work at risk if the worktree is cleaned up; have it commit | | **CTX** | Context above 300k (amber) or 450k (red) tokens | It will slow down and forget earlier instructions. Have it wrap up and hand back, or re-dispatch the rest fresh | | **ORPHAN** | A detached process is still running from its worktree. Grey while the agent is still working (usually it is polling its own `nohup` run); red once the agent goes quiet or finishes | Kill it once you're sure nothing needs it | | **DRIFT** | The judge says it is drifting (below), and you haven't dismissed it | See below | | **STUCK** | The judge says it is stuck (below), and you haven't dismissed it | See below | ### Judge verdicts The **JUDGE** column shows the latest verdict from the optional [LLM check](#the-judge-optional-on-by-default). It is a small model's opinion of the brief against the last 40 actions, so treat it as a prompt to look, not a fact. The detail view (`enter`) shows what the agent is doing, the judge's concern, and how the verdict has changed over time. | Verdict | Means | What to do | |---|---|---| | ✓ **on track** | Its recent actions serve the brief's steps, even if slowly | Nothing | | ↯ **drifting** (amber, adds **DRIFT**) | It is doing work the brief doesn't ask for, widening scope, or breaking a rule the brief states (running tests in the background when told to run them in the foreground, editing files it was told not to touch). The concern names an action it can see; growth that still serves the brief, or a baseline taken on the base branch, doesn't count | Read the concern in the detail. If it is real, have the lead message the agent to get back to the brief, or stop it. If the extra work is fine (your brief was narrower than you meant), have the lead tell the agent so with `SendMessage`: the judge treats the lead's messages as part of the brief and checks again after the agent's next action. If it is a false alarm, press `d` to dismiss it | | ⟳ **stuck** (red, adds **STUCK**) | It repeats actions without progress, retries a failure without changing approach, or waits on something that won't come | Find the repeated failure in the feed. Give it the missing piece through the lead, or stop it and re-dispatch with a better brief. If it is a false alarm, press `d` to dismiss it | | ? **unclear** | Too little activity to tell | Nothing; wait | | … **judging** | A check is in progress | Nothing | | blank | Not judged yet (it needs 5 tool calls), or the judge is off | Nothing | Verdicts refresh at most every 3 min per agent, after 5 more tool calls. Press `j` to re-check the selected agent now, for example after the lead has nudged it. Finished agents are never judged; their last verdict stays, greyed out, and DRIFT and STUCK are dropped. **Dismissing.** `d` on a drifting or stuck agent marks that verdict as dismissed: it shows greyed out as "· dismissed", DRIFT or STUCK goes away, the nudge leaves the concern out, and the next check lists it to the judge as a concern you've cleared, so it shouldn't be raised again on the same actions. A new concern flags as usual. `d` again restores the verdict. ## The judge (optional, on by default) Rules catch mechanical failures. For drift, `tracon` periodically asks a small model (Claude Haiku 5.5) to read an agent's brief, the lead'
